learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Committed true cost 1 to A from supplied roads: S-A 2, S-B 3, B-A refund 2, A-C 2.
observations.exploration: Settled S, A, B, C in cheapest-label order. Labels finished A 2, B 3, C 4. First full-road pass changed A to 1 while C stayed 4; second changed C to 3. No reset or editable road offered.
observations.reveal: Confirmed cost 1 and traced locked A preventing later improvement, then the delayed propagation to C on the second pass. Named Bellman-Ford and extra checks.
observations.visual: Actual 1257 by 936 dark screenshots inspected. Parallel directed maps show locked versus revisable labels, numbered roads and highlighted updates. Reveal moved the upper map partly out of view; inner scrolling exposed the explanation.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner explicitly said learning history and analytics not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, metadata or other reviewer judgments inspected.

prediction.reason: Concrete route arithmetic elicits an answer before algorithm execution.

interaction.reason: Stepping both methods shows the failure and delayed downstream correction.

payoff.reason: Explanation links the visible failure to the settled-label assumption.

clarity.reason: Numbered roads, locks and parallel maps explain the contrast.
clarity.evidence: Pass order makes C correction take a second pass.

transfer.reason: General limitation named without a new map or modified condition.
transfer.evidence: All execution follows the same four-road graph.

surprise.reason: A later refund invalidates a seemingly final cheapest label.
surprise.evidence: A remains locked at 2 despite route cost 1.

visualExplanation.evidence: C corrected only on second pass.

depth.evidence: First pass fixes A, second C.
